title: From Crisis to Crisis Classic
author: Michael Bailey
description:
In 2009, Michael Bailey and Jeffrey Taylor started a show called From Crisis to Crisis: A Superman Podcast. Their mission was to talk about all of the Superman comics published between Man of Steel #1 in 1986 and Adventures of Superman #649 in 2006. They didn't quite get there but racked up an impressive 270 episodes and got all the way to the wedding. Back in 2025, Mike could no longer afford the hosting service that let the show continue to be listened to, but found this service and thought it would be a good way to get the show "back on the air" so to speak. 

So, whether you were a long time listener or have never heard an episode, here is the archive for From Crisis to Crisis. Listen to Mike and Jeff talk about Man of Steel (1986), The Supergirl Saga, Burn Out, Exile, The Brainiac Trilogy, Soul Search, Krisis of the Krimson Kryptonite, Time and Time Again, Blackout, Panic in the Sky, The Blaze/Satanus War, The Death and Return of Superman, The Battle for/Fall of Metropolis, Peer Pressure, Dead Again, The Death of Clark Kent, The Trial of Superman, Final Night and the Wedding. All of that and so much more was covered in these episodes, plus all of the interviews the boys conducted as well.

From the mysteries of time and the meaning of energy to the relationship between mind, matter, and perception, each conversation invites a closer look at what seems familiar—and the unexpected questions hidden within it.

What do we mean when we say something is real? How does language influence what we think we understand? Where do scientific explanations, philosophical reasoning, and direct spiritual experience meet, and where do their approaches lead in different directions?

With curiosity, depth, and a willingness to reconsider, Shayne and Devan follow ideas through their possibilities and contradictions, distinguish evidence from interpretation, and explore how even our most cherished explanations might open into something we have yet to imagine.

Whether you have ADHD or love someone who does, we dive into practical tips for daily life, family dynamics, and support. title: True Crime and Serial Killers

title: The BLEND™ System Podcast
author: BLEND System LLC
description:
The BLEND™ Podcast is a three-episode limited series exploring the people, partnerships and innovations behind automated fuel additive dosing for bulk petroleum tankers. 


The series traces the Kirkpatrick family's trucking roots to 1938, explores AlumiTank's 37-year history and examines the operational and safety challenges of manual fuel additive handling that inspired the three-year development of the BLEND™ system. 


Featuring David Kirkpatrick, founder and CEO of BLEND System LLC and executive director of AlumiTank, and Nathaniel Doddridge, senior vice president of fuel operations at Casey's, the series explores how generations of industry experience and collaboration led to a new approach to fuel additive dosing. 


Through its partnership with Casey's, the BLEND™ system has been field-validated across more than 500 loads and 3.5 million gallons of fuel treated as of the time of publication, demonstrating the need to improve safety, precision and efficiency in bulk petroleum transportation.

title: Les Miserables by Victor Hugo
author: Arthur Lane
description:
France, 1815. Jean Valjean leaves prison after nineteen years in the galleys, sentenced for stealing a loaf of bread. Hardened and shunned by society, he finds his life changed by one unexpected act of mercy. He swears to become an honest man, but his past will not let him go. Inspector Javert, a relentless officer of the law who believes no criminal can change, pursues him for decades.

Hugo’s epic of redemption, justice and love moves from the provincial towns of France to the slums, sewers and barricades of Paris. Along the way we meet Fantine, the abandoned mother forced into ruin. There is Cosette, the orphan girl enslaved by the cruel Thénardier innkeepers, and Marius, the young idealist torn between love and revolution. Gavroche, the fearless street urchin, joins the student uprising as it builds toward the June Rebellion of 1832.

First published in 1862, Les Misérables is a monumental work of French literature and historical fiction. It inspired the world-famous musical and countless film adaptations, and it remains a powerful story of poverty, conscience, faith and the struggle for human dignity.

Whether you are discovering the story for the first time or returning to it after the stage show or the film, this unabridged audiobook gives you Victor Hugo’s masterpiece in full, from the first page to the last.

This edition presents the classic English translation by Isabel F. Hapgood, first published in 1887 and admired for its faithfulness to Hugo’s original French.

title: The College Life Guide
author: jchizek
description:
College is supposed to be some of the best years of your life, but that doesn’t mean it’s always easy. Have you ever felt stressed about classes, friendships, money, your future, or just trying to balance everything? Or maybe you just want to hear from other students who are going through the same things you are.
The College Life Guide, hosted by Jacob Chizek, is a weekly podcast made for college students, by college students. Each week, I bring on different guests to talk about their experiences and what college is really like. We cover everything from academics, friendships, stress, internships, and preparing for a career to going out, funny stories, mistakes, and the everyday ups and downs of being a college student.
As a college student myself, I understand a lot of the same things other students are dealing with because I’m going through them too. College has taught me that everyone has a different experience, and sometimes the best advice comes from hearing what other people have gone through. That’s why I started The College Life Guide—to give students a place to share their stories, advice, mistakes, and lessons they have learned along the way.
What makes The College Life Guide different is that it’s not just someone telling you how to succeed in college. It’s real students having real conversations about what college is actually like. Whether you’re already in college or getting ready to start, tune in each week for new stories, advice, laughs, and different perspectives on college life.

title: Per le altre | Chora Inchieste
author: Chora Media - Elisabetta Moro e Alessandra Vescio
description:
In Francia è da poco scoppiato il caso di Gisèle Pelicot quando le giornaliste Elisabetta Moro e Alessandra Vescio incontrano Anna, una delle donne che ha deciso di raccontare la sua storia,che, per certi versi, somiglia molto a quella di Pelicot.

Per sottomissione chimica si intende la somministrazione di sostanze a propria  insaputa, per ridurre la capacità di reagire e permettere l’abuso.

In Italia se ne parla poco, come se la violenza non esistesse.

In questo podcast, Elisabetta Moro e Alessandra Vescio indagano il fenomeno nel nostro Paese. Attraverso le voci di Anna, Stefania e Diana, che hanno scelto di condividere le loro esperienze, raccontano storie di fiducia tradita, dolore e giustizia mancata.

Ma raccontano anche altro: la fatica di essere credute, la forza di ricostruirsi e la determinazione di queste donne a rompere il silenzio, per sé e per tutte quelle a cui è successo e che non sono riuscite a parlarne. Perché ciò che resta invisibile non può essere riconosciuto né prevenuto. E perché cominciare a parlarne è il primo passo per cambiare lo sguardo: da chi subisce a chi agisce la violenza.


Le notizie dicono cosa è successo. Chora Inchieste prova a spiegare cosa c’è dietro. Ogni mese, circa, un’inchiesta per scoprire un lato inedito dell’attualità.

title: Alone, but READY
author: Alone
description:
It's 3am. The case is yours, the room is quiet, and there's no one left to ask. This is the moment every anesthesia resident trains for — and it's exactly the moment this podcast prepares you for.
Alone, But Ready is a podcast for anesthesia residents and trainees who want to do more than memorize facts for an exam. It's for the doctor who wants to truly understand — so that when the pressure is on and the decision is theirs alone, they can manage the case with calm, clinical confidence.
Here's what makes this show different: every topic is taught from the anesthesia point of view. We don't just study a disease, a drug, or a procedure the way a textbook or another specialty would. We ask the questions that actually matter in the OR:
Why is the surgeon doing this procedure, and what is their goal for the patient?
How does that procedure change the physiology you're responsible for?
What does it mean for your anesthetic plan — your airway, your hemodynamics, your drugs, your monitoring?
How do you manage the situation to minimize complications and help the patient get the full benefit of their surgery?
This is the difference between remembering a concept and being able to apply it. Between knowing what to do and understanding why you're doing it. And that "why" is what holds steady when you're on your own at 3am.
In each episode, you'll get clinically grounded breakdowns of the topics that matter, real-world case reasoning that walks through how an experienced anesthetist actually thinks, and the kind of practical, connect-the-dots teaching that turns scattered facts into sound clinical judgment. We focus on the why behind every decision, because that's what makes knowledge usable when it counts.
Whether you're prepping for exams, starting your first solo cases, or simply tired of memorizing without understanding, this podcast is built to make you a more confident, more capable, and safer anesthesiologist — one episode at a time.
Because the goal was never just to pass. The goal is to walk into any room, on any night, and know that you're ready.
Subscribe to Alone, But Ready — and turn your late-night studying into the quiet confidence to manage any case, even at 3am.
New episodes regularly. Built for residents. Focused on the why.

title: The age of humanoid robots

They are becoming a reality through remarkable developments in artificial intelligence, robotics, machine learning, and engineering. From robots that can walk and communicate to machines capable of performing complex physical tasks, technology is bringing humanity closer to a future where robots may become part of everyday life.

Beyond Human: The Age of Humanoid Robots explores the fascinating evolution of humanoid robotics and its potential impact on society. This two-episode podcast examines how humanoid robots developed, the technologies that make them possible, and the companies leading this technological revolution.

The series also investigates how robots could transform industries such as healthcare, manufacturing, education, and domestic services. However, technological progress also raises important questions about employment, privacy, safety, human relationships, and ethical responsibility.

Are humanoid robots designed to assist humanity, or could they eventually compete with humans in different areas of life? What happens when machines become increasingly capable of thinking, learning, and interacting like people?

Join us as we explore the opportunities, challenges, and unanswered questions surrounding one of the most exciting technological developments of our time.

title: The Dark Epoch: Quest for the LightSeeker
author: Trent Cucchiarelli
description:
Eight years ago, the LightSeeker vanished, leaving behind a world divided by fear, faith and uncertainty.
In the powerful kingdom of Ecclesium, the ruling Triarchy maintains order through the Unity, while an ancient order of Paladins searches for the one figure believed capable of restoring balance.
But as their quest unfolds, long-buried secrets begin to surface, threatening everything they believe about their world.
In The Dark Epoch, magic is unlike anything you've encountered before. Memories can be explored, minds can be entered, and even the boundaries of time can be challenged. But when memories can be manipulated, how can anyone be certain of the truth?
Blending epic fantasy with psychological mystery, Quest for the LightSeeker is a story of loyalty, betrayal, identity and the consequences of choices that echo across time.
Inspired by the rich worlds of traditional fantasy and the mind-bending mysteries of science fiction, this is an adventure where nothing is quite as it seems, and even the smallest detail may hold the key to everything.
Written and narrated by Trent Cucchiarelli, this complete 15-hour fantasy audiobook is available free, released chapter by chapter as a podcast.

title: The Path of Prosperity
author: James Allen
description:
James Allen confronts the harsh realities of life, revealing a profound journey into the human condition. In *The Path of Prosperity*, he begins with an unsettling observation: sorrow blankets the world, and suffering burns through the lives of many. But instead of seeking blame externally, Allen dives deep within himself, uncovering the root causes of these struggles. This audiobook invites listeners to explore the transformative power of self-awareness and personal responsibility.

At its core, this work presents the Law of Love, a guiding principle that can reshape our lives when embraced fully. Allen challenges us to rethink our mindset and actions, suggesting that true prosperity stems from inner harmony and positive adjustment to life’s inevitable trials. Through this journey, listeners will engage with timeless ideas about character, purpose, and the essence of happiness.

As you navigate Allen's insights, you'll uncover practical wisdom on how to cultivate resilience and foster meaningful connections. Each chapter offers a deeper understanding of how thoughts shape our reality, urging you to take charge of your mental landscape. Join Allen as he lights the path toward a more fulfilling life, one that is rich with purpose and love. Discover the strength within you to change your circumstances and embrace the journey toward prosperity. Tune in and let Allen's words stir your spirit and inspire your quest for a better life.

author: Tes Macpherson
description:
Are you an expert with an approach of your own? Maybe a consultant, coach, mentor, adviser or business book author. Are you worried about what AI means for your business? You’re not alone.  
I’m Tes Macpherson. I’ve spent thirty years designing software systems for corporates and startups, and the last five focusing on solo coaches and consultants. In short, five-minute episodes, I tackle the problems you face in packaging and delivering your service. Think feast or famine, being maxed out, and not knowing where to start with AI. And I show you how to blend AI into the way you work without losing what makes you unique.  
I don’t want a world where expertise is being highjacked by Big Tech just like our high streets are now filled with generic chain stores. I want a world full of artisans: independent experts whose way of doing things stays visible, valued and vouched for. That future is possible, but only if we build it on purpose.  Hit follow, and let’s build it together.

Explore disaster preparedness, survival techniques, emergency food storage, water purification, off-grid living, backup power systems, bug-out bags, survival gear, home security, and emergency communications. description:
Everyone Has a Story.

Life is short. We hear it all the time, but how often do we really stop and think about what it means?

Join husband and wife Byron and Amy as they share real stories about life, love, family, faith, laughter, heartbreak, and everything in between.

Inspired by a family motto born from an incredible story of survival, Life Is Short, Party Everyday is about embracing the time we're given, finding joy even during life's toughest moments, and recognizing that everyone has a story worth telling.

From their own personal experiences to conversations with everyday people who have extraordinary stories, Byron and Amy bring humor, honesty, hope, and heart to every episode.

Some stories will make you laugh. Others might make you cry. And some just might change the way you look at life.

Because your story matters. And so does every day we're given.

Join me for a deep dive into unpopular opinions, heartfelt conversations about love, heartbreak, and everything in between. Ready for some candid chats and eye-opening insights? description: Asphalt plays a part in everyone's lives. For some, it's simply the surface they drive and park on. For others, it's something they don't give a second thought to. For others, it's their life. Wherever you fall on this spectrum, this podcast is for you. Brought to you by HSC Pavement Maintenance, Layers of Asphalt isn't filled with industry jargon or obscure statistics. It's a unique look at asphalt, and the people who have dedicated their lives to it. New episodes every Tuesday.

title: Builders of Faith: Daniel and Revelation, the Podcast
author: Builders of Faith
description: Join Builders of Faith and LS Baker Jr. for an in-depth study of Daniel and Revelation. Explore their prophecies, symbols, and historical context while learning how to let Scripture interpret Scripture. Each episode builds a foundation for understanding these two biblical books, revealing their connections and keeping Jesus Christ at the center. Discover what their messages meant then—and what they mean for our faith and lives today.

title: The A1c Turnaround Podcast
author: Charles Kirkland
description:
If your numbers no longer match your effort, this podcast is for you.
In November 2025, Charles Kirkland blacked out. His labs: A1c 7.2%, triglycerides 1,761, blood pressure 192/114. Working with his doctors, he brought his A1c down to 5.7% and his triglycerides to 144 — by learning to read the numbers he’d ignored for years. 
The A1c Turnaround is where he teaches you to read yours.
Plain-English conversations about metabolic syndrome and type 2 diabetes: A1c and blood sugar, triglycerides and cholesterol, blood pressure, insulin resistance, fatty liver, belly fat, sleep, and inflammation — without fad diets, wellness hype, or impossible routines. 
Built on the Four Loads framework from Charles’s book, The A1c Turnaround: The Journey Back.
For adults over 40 whose labs don’t match how hard they’re trying.
Free download — The Kitchen Table Numbers Sheet, the one-page guide to the numbers that matter: metabolicclaritylabs.com
Metabolic Clarity Labs

title: Player Two Podcast
author: Player Two Podcast

Hosted by Jay and Greg, we have real-world discussions covering everything from retro and current games, to fantasy football strategy, and everyday issues. Whether we're analyzing major industry releases, debating anime story arcs, or breaking down sports and entertainment news, we may not be experts, but we keep the conversation straightforward. author: Daniel Peter
description:
How did our upbringing shape us? Welcome to The African Perspective: How We Were Raised.
We explore the powerful, funny, and profound stories, traditions, and lessons from our African childhoods. This show is about family, identity, and legacy. We unpack lessons from our parents, grandparents, and the community that raised us. We’ll discuss the pressure of expectation of being African discuss unlearning some unhealthy character learned from our messed up childhood, navigating the diaspora, and the rich cultures that make up the continent.
Subscribe for honest conversations that is impactful.

description: You know you're not the voice in your head. You've read the books. And then you have a bad day, and the voice runs the show again. Chrysalis is a live show about what happens next. Each week, real people practice Moment Mindfulness with me on the air. You hear what changes for them. You hear where they get stuck. And you hear the moment the voice stops feeling like them. I'm Dr. Mark Waller, a marriage and family therapist for 30 years. Start the practice yourself with the first chapter of my book, Free of the Mind, free: masteringthought.com/free-chapter

title: Iron Crew WW2: inside the crew stations of America's fighting machine
author: Iron Crew WW2
description: WWII documentaries from inside the crew stations of America's fighting machines, in the air, on land, and sea. What it was actually like to do the job. In the air: the B-17 waist gunner at an open window at fifty below zero. On land: the Sherman loader feeding a red-hot breech. At sea: the submarine crew holding still under depth charges, and the coxswain driving a Higgins boat onto Omaha Beach. Every episode puts you in one seat. No battles refought from a map table. Just the cold, the noise, the equipment, the odds, and the men who lived with them. Our motto comes from the Marines' Hymn. The words "in the air" were added in 1942, in the middle of the war these crews fought. The line fits every one of them. Every episode is researched from unit records, Army, Air Forces and Navy manuals, and veteran accounts. Sources are listed in each video's description. If someone in your family served in one of these seats, tell us their position and unit in the comments. We read every one.

Welcome to "Bad Ideas," the podcast where seasoned business professionals dissect and revamp seemingly terrible business ideas. Through lively discussions and creative brainstorming, we transform these bad ideas into innovative, viable solutions. Tune in and witness the magic of turning bad ideas into extraordinary possibilities.

title: Can WeTalk About Work Podcast
author: CanWeTalkAboutWork
description:
Can We Talk About Work? is a podcast about the conversations shaping work right now. Business, technology, leadership, culture, careers, AI, change, and the very human side of how work actually gets done.
We’ll go beyond headlines and polished talking points to explore what is changing, what it means, and what people should be paying attention to next. Some episodes will dig into big workplace shifts. Others will focus on the decisions, tensions, ideas, and experiences that rarely make it into formal conversations. Some might be more about sports.
You never know what you will get, and that’s how work is, too.
CWTAW won’t follow the same format every time. Some episodes might feature one-on-one conversations with guests. Some might bring together panels with different perspectives. Some might be solo episodes built around a question, trend, story, or moment worth unpacking. Sometimes the best conversation needs a room full of voices. Sometimes it only needs one.
The format may change, but the point stays the same: thoughtful, candid conversations that help make sense of work without pretending there is always an easy answer.
Business. Tech. Leadership. Life. Can we talk about work?

title: A More Dangerous Game: The Podcast
author: Jay Weiner
description:
A young sportswriter. Patty Hearst. A surprise birthday party. The FBI. Four months in federal prison.


Fifty years later, veteran journalist Jay Weiner looks back at the extraordinary events behind his coming-of-age memoir, A More Dangerous Game: How a Young Sportswriter Met Patty Hearst and Landed in Federal Prison.


In these short, first-person episodes, he shares behind-the-scenes stories, historical context, and reflections that go beyond the pages of the book. Along the way, he explores sports, politics, loyalty, betrayal, mistakes, and resilience.

From call stories and protocol changes to dispatch chaos, hospital handoffs, police encounters, firehouse stereotypes, management nonsense, burnout, and the stuff you wish you could say on the radio, nothing is safe from the debrief.
No patient details. No agency names. No pretending this job is normal. Just EMS stories, dark humor, salty banter, and a clinically concerning amount of caffeine.

title: Cosy Lounge Podcast

description:
Hello and welcome to The Cosy Lounge!

title: Headamentals
author: Rhett Power
description:
Self-Talk Isn't Just Personal. It's Organizational.
What if one of the most important leadership skills is something we've barely been talking about?
We spend enormous amounts of time teaching leaders how to communicate, motivate, manage performance, and build great cultures. But how much time do we spend teaching them how to talk to themselves?
And what happens when those internal conversations begin shaping the teams they lead?
Welcome to Headamentals, hosted by six-time entrepreneur, bestselling author, and executive coach Rhett Power.
Every week, Rhett challenges conventional thinking about leadership by exploring how self-talk influences decision-making, confidence, communication, accountability, trust, and organizational culture.
Drawing on his book Headamentals: How Leaders Can Defeat Negative Self-Talk, the 3-C Maverick Method—Catch, Confront, Change—and years of building businesses and coaching leaders around the world, Rhett explores the leadership conversation we're missing.
At a time when AI, economic uncertainty, and constant organizational change are putting enormous pressure on people, understanding our internal conversations matters more than ever.
This isn't about pretending everything is positive or eliminating difficult thoughts. It's about developing the self-awareness, judgment, and behaviors that help leaders and teams thrive.
Better Self-Talk. Better Leaders. Better Teams.
This podcast is for leadership education and personal development. It is not a substitute for professional mental health care.

title: Lessons with Darrow
author: Disciple Nations Alliance
description:
The ideas that shaped history still have the power to shape our future.


Join Christian author, teacher, and Disciple Nations Alliance co-founder Darrow Miller as he explores the power of biblical truth to transform lives, cultures, and nations. In season one, Darrow asks: How can we revive the Reformation today? 


Drawing from Scripture, history, and over five decades of ministry around the world, Darrow unpacks the biblical ideas that shaped civilizations, cultivated free and just societies, and laid the only foundation for human flourishing.


From the Reformation to the pressing challenges facing our world today, discover how a biblical worldview can equip ordinary Christians to become agents of change in their communities and nations.


What if the greatest ideas for transforming our world aren't new at all?

title: Rabbithole Road Trip
author: Bri Watson
description:
Some podcasts have a studio. Some have a script. This one has a car, a full tank of gas (hopefully), and absolutely no idea where the conversation might end up.

Hosted by Bri, Rabbithole Road Trip takes the conversation out of the studio and onto the open road. From everyday absurdities and unexpected discoveries to random conversations, questionable detours, and whatever else comes up along the way, nothing is particularly off-limits, and very little goes according to plan.

Along for the ride are occasional guests, familiar voices, and whoever else happens to get caught up in the madness.

There’s no itinerary, no carefully manufactured moments, and definitely no promise that we’ll stay on topic.

Just real conversations, unexpected moments, and the occasional wrong turn that turns out to be worth taking.

On Reddit vs. the Record, host Kimbyr brings three real threads to the table (the personal stories, the strange details, the comment-section back-and-forth) and puts them up against the record: the history, science and documents you'd want to pull up mid-story.


By the end of the episode, you're not left with an answer. You're left with a better question: what do we want to accept as the truth? Reddit vs. the Record is a Rewind Original powered by PAVE Studios. New episodes every Thursday.

title: Organic Gardener's Composting (The Art of Sustainable Soil)
author: Steve Solomon
description:
Steve Solomon dives straight into the world of composting, revealing how this simple practice can transform your garden and your approach to growing food. Whether you’re a novice or a seasoned gardener, you'll discover the essential ingredients of successful composting, broken down into easy-to-follow steps. The audiobook not only covers the fundamental techniques but also explores the fascinating science behind decomposition, making it both informative and entertaining.

What sets this audiobook apart is its deep dive into vermiculture—composting with red worms. Solomon shares practical tips and tricks for harnessing these little powerhouses to enrich your soil. You’ll learn how to build your own composting units tailored to your space and needs, making this a hands-on guide that encourages experimentation.

But it’s not just about the how-to; Solomon intertwines the rich history of the organic gardening movement, connecting past practices to modern sustainability efforts. With an annotated bibliography included, you’ll have a roadmap to further explore the vast landscape of composting and food gardening.

Join Solomon on this journey to cultivate not just your garden, but a deeper understanding of nature's cycles. Get ready to dig into the art and science of composting and watch your gardening skills flourish!

From DDD and ALTCS to HCBS, foster care, adoption, and disability benefits, the paperwork, approvals, and endless waiting can make anyone want to lose it!

Through honest conversations, real-life experiences, humor, and a little frustration, we tackle the challenges of raising children with special needs and fighting for the support they deserve.

No judgment. No sugarcoating. Just real moms, real stories, and the freedom to lose it!

Because when you need permission for everything, sometimes you just need Permission to Lose It!

Buying a home is harder than it used to be. Prices are higher, mortgage rates have changed the monthly-payment math, starter homes are harder to find, and first-time buyers are entering the market later than ever.
But hard doesn't mean impossible.
Homebuyer Advantage is for people who want to understand the market, make smarter decisions, and buy a home with a real strategy.
When I was actively selling homes every week, I noticed that certain buyers were simply better prepared. They understood their finances, knew the market, had the right team around them, and understood the buying process. Those buyers had an advantage.
That's the Homebuyer Advantage.
In this podcast, we'll break down affordability, mortgages, monthly payments, neighborhoods, inspections, negotiating, choosing an agent and lender, knowing when you're overpaying, and everything else you need to make a confident homebuying decision.
The goal isn't to convince you to buy a house.
It's to make sure that when the time is right for you, you know exactly what you're doing.

title: How Supermarkets Lie about Cooking Oils
author: Nath Ji
description:
Walking down the grocery aisle shouldn't feel like decoding a chemistry textbook—yet food labels are designed to hide what is really inside the bottle. How Supermarkets Lie About Cooking Oils is a complete audio guide exposing the truth behind everyday kitchen fats, processed snack ingredients, and misleading "heart-healthy" marketing claims.

​In this guide, we strip away confusing jargon and show you how to inspect ingredient lists, spot hidden industrial seed oils, and choose traditional, heat-stable cooking fats for your home.

​Key topics covered:

• Industrial Oils to Avoid: Partially hydrogenated fats (vanaspati), refined palm olein, hexane-extracted cottonseed oil, and high-Omega-6 soybean and corn oils.

• Healthy Traditional Alternatives: A2 Bilona Desi Cow Ghee, cold-pressed Kachi Ghani Mustard Oil, unrefined Virgin Coconut Oil, Chekku Groundnut Oil, and Extra Virgin Olive Oil.

• The Deceptive Label Decoder: What terms like "Edible Vegetable Oil," "Blended Vegetable Oil," "0g Trans Fat," and "Interesterified Fat" actually mean on the back of a package.

Aquí hablamos del programa Au Pair en USA de manera detallada y sin romantizarlo: las normas y leyes que lo rigen, los retos y las fallas reales del sistema, y la mentalidad que te ayuda a vivirlo de la mejor manera posible.


En cada episodio encuentras: 

• Cómo funciona el programa Au Pair en Estados Unidos: requisitos, reglas y leyes explicadas de forma clara.

• Los retos reales y las fallas que presenta el programa, para que llegues con expectativas honestas. 

• Cómo elegir a tu Host Family y convivir con ella sin perderte en el camino. 

• La mentalidad y la adaptación cultural que hacen la diferencia en el día a día. 


Soy Yanimar Best, ex-Au Pair: viví 6 años y medio con mi Host Family y llevo 8 años viviendo en Estados Unidos, ligada al mundo Au Pair. Además trabajé 2 años como LCC (Local Community Counselor), acompañando de cerca a host families y au pairs durante su tiempo juntos. Hoy doy mentorías a futuras y actuales au pairs que quieren vivir su experiencia sin sentirse solas ni perdidas en el proceso.

Suscríbete para que aprendas de este mundo y sepas con mayor claridad si es algo que quieres intentar o no.

[Y si quieres acompañamiento, escríbeme por https://forms.gle/wdh9BivFk29Rovr17 para conocer mis mentorías.]
